## Design

### 2026-10-31: In this session I finished the schematic of my project. It wasn't too complicated, but it was my first time making a project schematic without a guide. In total, there is an ESP32 (where everything is

**4h**

In this session I finished the schematic of my project. It wasn't too complicated, but it was my first time making a project schematic without a guide. In total, there is an ESP32 (where everything is connected to), an encoder (to change the pages and do actions on the screen), a 1x8 connector (for the screen), and an AO3401A switch for the backlight LED. This is how the final schematic turned out:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.37.29 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/97d52ea04f8e0920fa86a88f3a15cfa53b644d028d0a62b5fdbede1712c25080.png)

I first started with the ESP32. After running the Electrical Rules Checker, I realized that I had to add a power flag to the +3V3 and GND.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.36.43 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/f196e977c61f438326ce7b381bd6069dca4747118fe616c7ecb388b7a3b43fe9.png)

Then, I did the 1x8 connector. I also added a small capacitor to kind of act like a tiny battery in case the screen redraws.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.31.53 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/efca96a22a1ffc12c72f2d2acc0c4f297f28ce162d7f6d8dce5910a7b46785dc.png)

Then, I added the AO3401A switch. This took a bit of time since I didn't really understand how it worked, but I ended up also adding a small resistor to limit the current.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.32.05 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/0c925e519be0fef2e85306f7b4962e9616a8d2d6e13d00be9c16b4251bb49b63.png)

Finally, I added an encoder. This was pretty simple since I used encoders in last week's project. I'm using the switch functionality along with the turning (the turning will change pages on the screen and the clicking will do an action). This is how it turned out:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.32.13 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/309172e650587838c078e4c54190251c45517cae58bc214cc413a342e16e2041.png)

Finally, I added the footprints to everything. I also decided to include some mounting holes in the end.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.53.58 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/b4a7ef99c69e3f17423bfe71e4ab52103e41855b37f5241c6ec0e50dab8844c5.png)

Next session I will finish the PCB and all the wiring.
